issues.title: Are the SD-CWT Key Binding Token / SD-JWT key binding really necessary for use in MLS?
issues.author: rohanmahy
issues.body:
The Key Binding Token in SD-CWT provides the following functions:

- prove possession of the holder private key
- sign the specific set of disclosures used
- to prevent replay of the SD-CWT when a cnonce is present
- explicitly set the audience (ex: the room) if none is set 
- potentially have a smaller validity period than the CWT it contains
- include other holder-asserted claims

MLS provides a signature over the LeafNodeTBS struct and includes a signature key that needs to match the holder key in the SD-CWT. Replaying just an SD-CWT would be impossible without signing the LeafNode. It would also implicitly bind the audience to the the current MLS group (although not to an application-level structure like a MIMI room). In this way, we might be able to get away without having a KBT.

Likewise an SD-JWT can contain an optional key binding token. The signature over the LeafNodeTBS struct covers the signature key and that needs to match the holder key in the SD-JWT.

issues.title: Mention that an SD-JWT can contain a regular JWT
issues.author: rohanmahy
issues.body:
From [Section 4.1](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-oauth-selective-disclosure-jwt-22.html#name-issuer-signed-jwt)

"An SD-JWT has a JWT component that MUST be signed using the Issuer's private key. It MUST NOT use the none algorithm."

In other words, most JWTs can be conveyed as an SD-JWT with no changes.

comments.author: rohanmahy
comments.body: now that the binding token is required, most JWTs could not be conveyed. Closing.

issues.title: -03: binding to the MLS signature key, a verification procedure, and the audience
issues.author: MarkAtwood
issues.body:
Reading -03 while assaying MLS credentials for mimid (from the remote MIMI interop table at the IETF 127 hackathon), a few gaps:

1. **Key binding.** Using the MLS signature key as the confirmation key is only "encouraged" (§3). If the cnf key is some other key, nothing binds the LeafNode's signature key to the token, which is the first Authentication Service requirement the draft quotes from RFC 9750. Requiring cnf to be the LeafNode's (or ExternalSender's) signature key would close it, or the draft could define another binding.
2. **Verification.** There's no procedure for a member checking a credential. That would cover the issuer's signature and how its key is found and trusted, the KBT signature under cnf, the audience, time validity against the LeafNode lifetime and KeyPackage reuse, and which claims identify the user.
3. **Audience.** "A representation of the MLS group" or a higher-level structure has no encoding: the group_id bytes, a room URI? Without one, a KBT made for one group verifies in another.
4. **"Same client."** RFC 9750 requirement 3 needs a rule for comparing two sd_cwt credentials: subject alone, or issuer and subject?
5. **Codepoint.** The suggested 0x0005 is also listed for weak-multi (draft-barnes-mls-addl-creds-01) in your codepoint coordination gist.
6. **Editorial.** "zero of more" (§3); the member-secrets reference renders as "\*\*\* BROKEN REFERENCE \*\*\*"; mimi-protocol is cited at -06 (now -07); §4 and §5 are TODO.

comments.author: MarkAtwood
comments.body:
One more, which we hit implementing a credential type of our own (draft-atwood-mls-didwebvh-credential) in mimid:

7. **`sd_jwt` isn't one vector.** The `sd_jwt` arm of `Credential` is `SdJwt`, which starts with a `Bool` and, when compacted, carries five fields. A party that doesn't support `sd_jwt` (a DS, a hub, a member before it upgrades) can't skip it, because there's no length that says where the credential ends: it reads the next field of the LeafNode from inside the credential. OpenMLS and mls-rs both carry a credential type they don't know as a single `opaque<V>`, so neither could carry this encoding. `sd_cwt` (`opaque sd_kbt<V>`) is fine. Wrapping the arm as `opaque sd_jwt<V>` holding the TLS encoding of `SdJwt` would fix it; that's what we did for did_webvh in -01.
